title: Lesson 25 - GDPR-compliant data model: identify, classify, protect personal and sensitive information; right to erasure
description: Given a customer scenario, recommend an approach for designing a General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) compliant data model, discussing the various options to identify, classify, and protect personal and sensitive information, including the right to erasure.

questions.question: A customer must honor erasure requests but is legally required to retain transaction history for seven years. What is the best erasure approach?
options: Hard-delete all records for the data subject
Anonymize/pseudonymize the personal fields while retaining the transactional records
Ignore the request due to retention law
Archive everything to a Big Object and delete nothing
questions.explanation: Anonymization satisfies erasure of personal data while preserving legally required transaction records; hard delete (A) conflicts with retention, ignoring (C) is non-compliant, and archive-only (D) leaves personal data intact.

questions.question: Which TWO platform capabilities directly protect personal data at rest and in access control?
options: Shield Platform Encryption for sensitive fields
Field-level security and permission sets to restrict access
questions.explanation: Shield Platform Encryption (A) and FLS/permission sets (B) are direct protection controls; read-only layouts and duplicate rules are not protection controls.

questions.question: Why can free-text fields be a compliance risk in a GDPR data model?
options: They can contain personal or sensitive data that is not classified, encrypted, or erasable
They are excluded from erasure requests
questions.explanation: Free text often holds unclassified personal data, undermining classification, encryption, and erasure; the other options are inaccurate.
